correctness.rationale: Every well-rounded planar lattice has a basis of two shortest vectors (proven by centered-fundamental-parallelogram contradiction); the lift of the two proposed sites is an orthogonal index-two superlattice with covering radius exactly L/2. Cup-length of the torus excludes any covering by two open contractible metric balls of radius strictly less than L/2. Farthest points are precisely rectangular Voronoi corners modulo the original lattice. The inversion-quotient equivalence and density endpoints are rigorously derived. The standalone rational checker passed 5607 finite assertions in seven sample Gram shapes, used as corroboration rather than proof.

value.rationale: This computes a motivated exact geodesic two-center covering invariant on an entire natural one-parameter family of flat tori, proves uniform sharpness of a topologically forced lower bound, and gives a sharp shape-dependent covering density interval with square and hexagonal equality classes. The quotient statement supplies an exact Chebyshev radius for nonrectangular flat pillowcase cone spheres. These are structural moduli-wide facts, not isolated numerical or reparameterized calculations.
